title: Day-to-day cost per pupil in attendance, State measure
question: By the State's own measure, how has the district's day-to-day cost per pupil in attendance moved, and against other large unified districts?
finding: The State's current expense of education per pupil in average daily attendance was $12,148 in 2016-17 and $25,643 in 2023-24 (+111%), while attendance fell from 50,753 to 45,287 (-11%). Among unified districts with 20,000 or more in attendance it ranked 10 of 56 in 2016-17 and 3 of 43 in 2023-24 (middle that year: $18,747). The district reported 55.74% of that cost going to classroom pay in 2024-25 and 55.51% in 2025-26, against the Education Code minimum (section 41372) of 55% for unified districts.
how: CDE current-expense files (Excel), unified districts only; rank 1 = highest cost per pupil in attendance. Classroom-pay share from Form CA of the district's unaudited actuals.
limits: Attendance is not enrolment: chronic absence (on the schools page) lowers attendance and so raises cost per pupil in attendance. San Francisco wages and prices are high; the State formula adds money for low-income pupils and English learners. The 2014-15 and 2015-16 files are in an old Excel format that could not be read here.
